learner_notice: Commit one response before feedback appears. Exit misses may release one bounded function-specific repair and one fresh re-entry.

items.title: Prerequisite check: fixed-speed waves
items.prompt: A wave’s speed remains fixed while its frequency doubles. What happens to its wavelength?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Guided practice: photon energy
items.prompt: The frequency of a photon is tripled. How does its energy change?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Less help: compare visible colors
items.prompt: Compared with violet light in vacuum, red light has which combination?
options: Longer wavelength and lower photon energy
Longer wavelength and higher photon energy
Shorter wavelength and lower photon energy
Shorter wavelength and higher photon energy
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: On your own: classify a wavelength
items.prompt: Radiation has a vacuum wavelength near 0.1 nanometer. Which broad region is the best classification?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Near exit: compare two photons
items.prompt: Photon B has twice the frequency of photon A in vacuum. Which comparison is correct?
options: B has twice the wavelength and half the energy
B has half the wavelength and twice the energy
B has the same wavelength and twice the energy
B has half the wavelength and the same energy
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Changed-task exit: hold beam power fixed
items.prompt: Two monochromatic beams deliver equal total power. Beam B has photons with twice the energy of Beam A. How do their photon arrival rates compare?
options: B delivers twice as many photons per second
Both deliver the same number of photons per second
B delivers one quarter as many photons per second
B delivers half as many photons per second
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: use both proportionalities
items.prompt: If vacuum wavelength becomes three times larger, which pair follows?
options: Frequency becomes one third and photon energy becomes one third
Frequency triples and photon energy triples
Frequency is unchanged and photon energy triples
Frequency becomes one third and photon energy triples
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: use a new factor
items.prompt: Photon C has four times the frequency of photon D in vacuum. Which statement is correct?
options: C has four times the wavelength and one quarter the energy
C has one quarter the wavelength and one quarter the energy
C has one quarter the wavelength and four times the energy
C has the same wavelength and four times the energy
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: connect power and count
items.prompt: At fixed beam power, photon energy decreases to one half. What happens to photon rate?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: change wavelength at fixed power
items.prompt: A beam’s wavelength is halved while total power is unchanged. What happens to photon energy and photon rate?
options: Energy halves and photon rate halves
Energy doubles and photon rate doubles
Energy is unchanged and photon rate halves
Energy doubles and photon rate halves
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Prerequisite check: add in-phase waves
items.prompt: Two waves of amplitude A reach the same point in phase. What is their combined amplitude at that instant?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Guided practice: integer path difference
items.prompt: Two coherent rays arrive with path difference 3λ. What interference is expected?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Less help: half-integer path difference
items.prompt: Two equal-amplitude coherent rays arrive with path difference 5λ/2. What outcome follows?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: On your own: change slit separation
items.prompt: In a Young double-slit setup, slit separation doubles while wavelength and screen distance remain fixed. What happens to fringe spacing?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Near exit: change wavelength
items.prompt: A double-slit experiment switches to light with twice the wavelength while L and d remain fixed. What happens to fringe spacing?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Changed-task exit: count reflection phase
items.prompt: Two reflected rays have negligible travel-phase difference. Only the first reflection is from lower to higher refractive index, producing a half-cycle reversal. For equal amplitudes, what is expected?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: isolate one geometry factor
items.prompt: In a double-slit setup, screen distance L triples while wavelength and slit separation stay fixed. How does fringe spacing change?
options: It becomes one third as large
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: change two factors
items.prompt: Wavelength is doubled and slit separation is also doubled, while screen distance stays fixed. What happens to fringe spacing?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: count reversals
items.prompt: Two reflected rays have equal travel phase. One ray undergoes a half-cycle reflection reversal and the other does not. What is their relative phase?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: match two reversals
items.prompt: Two reflected rays have an integer-wavelength travel difference, and each reflection adds the same half-cycle reversal. What is the net interference?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Prerequisite check: inverse wave variables
items.prompt: Wave speed stays fixed while frequency decreases. What happens to wavelength?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Guided practice: narrow the slit
items.prompt: A single slit becomes narrower while wavelength remains fixed. What happens to the angular diffraction pattern?
options: It disappears because no wave passes
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Less help: change wavelength
items.prompt: Two waves pass through identical slits. Wave B has the longer wavelength. Which wave diffracts through the larger angle?
options: Wave A, because shorter waves always spread more
Both spread equally because slit width matches
Neither wave, because diffraction requires a grating
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: On your own: identify grating control
items.prompt: In a diffraction grating, which quantity most directly sets the angles of principal orders for fixed wavelength?
options: The regular spacing between adjacent openings
The total photon energy stored in the screen
The color of the opaque support alone
The source’s distance from every detector
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Near exit: compare visible spreading
items.prompt: Red and blue light pass through the same narrow slit. Which pattern has the wider central maximum?
options: Blue, because blue has the shorter wavelength
Both are identical because both are visible
Neither, because single slits cannot diffract light
Red, because red has the longer wavelength
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Changed-task exit: shift an X-ray peak
items.prompt: For fixed lattice spacing and diffraction order, the X-ray wavelength increases. How does the peak angle change?
options: The peak becomes a sound resonance
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: use the aperture ratio
items.prompt: Which change increases λ/a for a single slit?
options: Decrease wavelength and increase slit width
Keep wavelength fixed and increase slit width
Increase wavelength and decrease slit width
Decrease wavelength while slit width stays fixed
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: change aperture only
items.prompt: A slit width is reduced to one half at fixed wavelength. Which qualitative change follows?
options: The wave stops superposing with itself
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: isolate the peak equation
items.prompt: At fixed lattice spacing d and order n, which change requires a larger diffraction angle in 2d sinθ = nλ?
options: A lower order with wavelength fixed
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: change lattice spacing
items.prompt: For fixed X-ray wavelength and diffraction order, lattice spacing d increases. How does the peak angle change?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Prerequisite check: orient the triad
items.prompt: Electric field points +x and magnetic field points +y. Using the stated right-hand orientation from E toward B, which way does the wave propagate?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Guided practice: classify linear polarization
items.prompt: At one location, the electric field oscillates back and forth along a fixed vertical line. Which polarization is described?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Less help: classify circular polarization
items.prompt: The electric-field magnitude remains constant while its direction rotates uniformly, tracing a circle. Which state is described?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: On your own: find the magnetic field
items.prompt: A wave propagates +z and its electric field points +x. Which magnetic-field direction completes the stated right-hand triad?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Near exit: select the valid triad
items.prompt: Which set is mutually perpendicular and has the correct right-hand orientation?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Changed-task exit: rotate a polarizer
items.prompt: Vertically linearly polarized light reaches an ideal linear polarizer whose axis is horizontal. What is transmitted ideally?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: enforce perpendicularity
items.prompt: Propagation is +x and electric field is +z. Which magnetic direction completes the right-hand orientation?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: solve a new triad
items.prompt: Electric field points −x and magnetic field points +y. Which propagation direction follows from the stated right-hand orientation?
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Repair: use the transmitted component
items.prompt: Which electric-field component does an ideal vertical linear polarizer transmit?
options: The component parallel to the vertical axis
The component perpendicular to the vertical axis
Only a component parallel to propagation
A component selected by photon energy alone
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.

items.title: Fresh re-entry: use crossed axes
items.prompt: Unpolarized light passes an ideal vertical polarizer and then an ideal horizontal polarizer. What leaves the second polarizer ideally?
options: Vertically polarized light at full transmitted amplitude
Light with twice the original photon frequency
items.directions: Choose the single option best supported by the stated facts.
